newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols up, low-delta calls sought.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols up, low-delta calls sought.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were well bid at midsession, despite the weekend time-decay factor, with good interest in deep out-of-the-money calls, dealers said.
They noted that volatilities were underpinned by uncertainties ahead of next Friday's September U.S. employment report and various other important economic data next week.

"It could be that we're getting into that eight-day window (prior to monthly employment report)," said a trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. He said volatilities had risen sharply just before each release of jobs data this year.

Implied volatility for December T-bond futures options was up 0.4 point to 10.4 percent, gradually rising from an opening of 10.1 percent. November volatility was up half a point on the day at 10.5 percent.
Large trades done in the CBOT pit this morning tended to be bullish on volatilities as well as on the underlying bond prices, traders said.
An investment bank was said to have bought 3,000 contracts of December 114 calls covered against futures, while another house was seen buying 2,500 contracts of March 120 calls.

Traders noted growing perception that a second-half economic forecast by the Federal Reserve was beginning to take hold and that the market's long-term downtrend from January highs could be bottoming.

"If what we're entering into right now is a period where there's going to be one camp that still feels the next Fed move would be a tightening and you have people beginning to think they would not tighten...then I think you're getting exactly what you need for volatility to start picking up," a eurodollar trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
Implied volatilities for eurodollar futures options were mostly steady, with December and March virtually unchanged at 11.6 and 15.4 percent respectively.

The CME trader noted that December, March and June futures were all hovering near their 200-day moving averages, with the March contract briefly rising above its average at 94.16 today, a positive longer-term signal.

Traders expected choppy trading next week, with a lot of economic data, kicking off with the Chicago Purchasing Management index and new home sales Monday and the National Purchasing Management index and leading indicators Tuesday.
"Next week is a big week of economic releases, and this market is in a number-to-number mode," said Charles Ovis, manager of global trading at EVEREN Securities.
"It creates an extremely volatile trading environment that is difficult to trade short-term, but the overall technical makeup in the market is fairly strong," he added.
